answers.answer: Endpoint: GET https://graph.mapillary.com/map_features. Parameters: bbox=minLon,minLat,maxLon,maxLat (left,bottom,right,top); object_values=<class>[,<class>...] (wildcards supported); fields=<comma list> (mandatory - every call must name its fields); limit (default and max 2000); optional date filters start_first_seen_at, end_first_seen_at, start_last_seen_at, end_last_seen_at (ISO 8601, e.g. 2022-08-16T16:42:46Z). Pagination: none documented for map_features (paging cursors are documented only for /images combined with creator_username). The official FAQ's answer to the 2000 cap is to split the bbox into smaller boxes (their example uses z18 tile bounds via mercantile) and loop. Bbox size: 'must be smaller than 0.01 degrees square' (formalised 16 Jan 2026). The wording is ambiguous (0.01 square degrees of area, or 0.01 deg per side); the docs' own sample bbox is 0.041 x 0.010 deg, which suggests an area limit. The model bbox is 0.032 x 0.016 deg = 0.000512 sq deg, so it probably fits in one call, but splitting into cells of at most 0.01 deg per side satisfies both readings. Rate limits: search APIs 10,000 requests/minute per app; entity APIs 60,000/minute per app; tiles 50,000/day. Over the limit, Graph returns error code 4 'Application request limit reached'. Secondary (forum): users report HTTP 500 timeouts on /map_features and /images even for small boxes, so retry with smaller cells.
answers.quote: bbox - float,float,float,float, filter map features in the bounding box. Specify in this order: left, bottom, right, top (or minLon, minLat, maxLon, maxLat).

answers.answer: Class identifier confirmed: object--street-light (name 'Street Light') in the official Points list; the same value appears in the Detections list. Neighbouring classes to keep apart: object--support--pole, object--support--utility-pole, object--traffic-light--* (cyclists, general-horizontal, general-single, general-upright, other, pedestrians). Map feature entity fields (Graph API): id; geometry (GeoJSON Point); object_value (string); object_type ('traffic_sign' or 'point'); first_seen_at and last_seen_at (ISO 8601 strings, e.g. "2021-12-23T03:24:54+0000", time of least/most recent contributing detection); aligned_direction (float, compass angle the object faces); images ({data:[{id, geometry}]}, with any Image field dot-selectable, e.g. fields=images.captured_at,images.is_pano,images.compass_angle). Date format differs by surface: Graph entity = ISO 8601 string; vector tiles = integer milliseconds since epoch; image captured_at = integer ms since epoch on both surfaces. No confidence/score field is documented for map features.
answers.quote: first_seen_at - string, ISO 8601 timestamp of the least recent detection contributing to this feature (e.g. "2021-12-23T03:24:54+0000").

answers.answer: Tile URL: https://tiles.mapillary.com/maps/vtp/mly_map_feature_point/2/{z}/{x}/{y}?access_token=TOKEN (Mapbox Vector Tile, pbf, XYZ scheme). Zoom: 14 only (minzoom = maxzoom = 14). Layer: 'point' (all non-sign classes in one layer; filter client-side on value == 'object--street-light'). Properties: id, value, first_seen_at, last_seen_at (both ms since epoch). Traffic signs are a separate tileset mly_map_feature_traffic_sign, layer 'traffic_sign'. Tiles do NOT carry aligned_direction, object_type or images; get those per feature from graph.mapillary.com/{id} or batch ?ids=. Simpler/more complete? For the 4 km2 model area: 4 tile requests versus 1-8 bbox calls - both are trivial; tiles avoid the bbox-size and 2000-cap questions but need an MVT decoder (mapbox_vector_tile, or mapillary-python-sdk map_feature_points_in_bbox with filter_values). For the whole city (~130 km2): roughly 11 x 11 = 121 z14 tiles (my estimate for a bbox around Timisoara), far under 50,000/day - tiles are clearly the simpler route and the one the docs recommend at scale. Whether a dense tile can silently drop features is not documented.
answers.quote: it is expected that clients use vector tiles for such use-cases at scale.

answers.answer: (a) Coverage tiles: https://tiles.mapillary.com/maps/vtp/mly1_public/2/{z}/{x}/{y}?access_token=TOKEN (original GPS positions) and https://tiles.mapillary.com/maps/vtp/mly1_computed_public/2/{z}/{x}/{y}?access_token=TOKEN (computed / map-matched positions; same schema). Layers: 'overview' z0-5 (Point); 'sequence' z6-14 (LineString; captured_at, creator_id, id = sequence id, image_id, organization_id, is_pano, quality_score); 'image' z14 only (Point; captured_at in ms since epoch, compass_angle, creator_id, id, sequence_id, organization_id, is_pano, quality_score). So 'was this street captured, and when' = z14 'image' points (or 'sequence' lines) snapped to street segments, using captured_at. (b) Graph API: GET https://graph.mapillary.com/images?bbox=minLon,minLat,maxLon,maxLat&fields=id,geometry,computed_geometry,captured_at,compass_angle,is_pano,sequence&limit=2000. Same bbox rule (smaller than 0.01 degrees square), limit default/max 2000, filters start_captured_at / end_captured_at (ISO 8601), is_pano, make, model. Pagination works only with creator_username, so with bbox you must split the box (or slice by capture date) whenever 2000 rows come back; a busy street easily exceeds 2000 images, so tiles are the more reliable source for coverage. Extra for the negative-evidence question: the detection search /images?fields=captured_at,detections.value&bbox=... returns per-image raw detections, which shows whether an image had detections at all.
answers.quote: Pagination is currently supported only in combination with creator_username parameter.

answers.answer: Steps: sign in to a Mapillary account, open https://www.mapillary.com/dashboard/developers, click 'Register Application', enter information about you and the app, then copy the 'Client Token'. Format: a string of the form MLY|<app id digits>|<32 hex chars> (the docs' example: MLY|0000000000000000000|9856ad9cc629a15337480e7344792d78). Passing it: either query parameter ?access_token=TOKEN (preferred for vector tiles) or header 'Authorization: OAuth TOKEN' (works for entity/Graph calls). Terms section 11 requires registering each application to obtain a client_id. Cost and waiting time are not stated in the official docs: the flow as described is self-service with no approval step, and no price is mentioned anywhere, but 'free' and 'instant' are not written down officially (see unconfirmed). The pipe characters should be URL-encoded as %7C when the token goes in a query string in some clients.
answers.quote: Click Register Application on the developer dashboard, and enter information about you and your app, then copy the client token to use it with the API.

answers.answer: What the Terms of Use (effective 15 Feb 2024) actually say: (1) CC BY-SA is stated for User Content, i.e. the images ('Your use of any User Content provided by other users is subject to the Creative Commons Share Alike (CC BY-SA) license, unless we indicate otherwise'); the help centre says 'All images on Mapillary are shared under a CC-BY-SA license'. No version number (4.0) is given in the Terms. (2) Machine-derived data (map features) is NOT explicitly placed under CC BY-SA; it is 'Content' owned by Mapillary and licensed under the Terms, with a specific attribution rule in section 11: visibly display the Mapillary logo and link back to the Mapillary homepage. (3) Section 11 also requires that an app 'materially supplement' Mapillary's services and not 'merely redistribute Content'. (4) Section 12 restricts commercial use to listed purposes. (5) Section 13 explicitly permits using Mapillary Services and all Content to develop, edit and contribute to OpenStreetMap / Overture; mapillary.com/osm adds that derived metadata may be published to OSM under the OSMF contributor terms and that attribution such as source=Mapillary is appreciated. (6) No rule about caching or storing API results was found in the Terms or the API docs; the docs themselves describe downloading map features as GeoJSON. Section 4/5 prohibits scraping by non-approved means, so stay on the API/tiles. Practical reading for the repo: a fused score per street segment that uses Mapillary points as one evidence source and shows the Mapillary logo + link (plus '(c) OpenStreetMap contributors', ODbL) is within the documented terms; committing the raw Mapillary export into a public MIT repo is the risky part - MIT covers the code only, so keep raw exports out of git (or in a data folder with its own notice) and ship the fetch script instead. ODbL compatibility of redistributing Mapillary-derived data outside OSM is not addressed officially.
answers.quote: you must attribute the source of the data by visibly displaying the Mapillary logo and linking back to the Mapillary homepage.

answers.answer: Official: a point map feature exists only if the object was detected in at least three images (two for traffic signs) and its position is triangulated; positional accuracy depends on the GPS accuracy of the capturing device; the web app calls them 'predicted locations'. No numeric accuracy, no confidence score and no per-class error rates are published officially. Consequence for the map: a street captured by a single sparse pass can have a real lamp and no map feature, so 'captured, no lamp detected' is only weak negative evidence, and a detection says a luminaire is visible (in daytime imagery), not that it works. Secondary (State of the Map 2022 talk by Said Turksever, benchmark against municipal street-light ground truth in Altinordu, Ordu): mean positional error 2.02 m (GoPro MAX), 2.17 m (GoPro Hero 7 Black), 2.21 m (iPhone 11); completeness 77.30 %, 87.57 %, 71.89 % respectively - i.e. 12-28 % of real lamps missed even with purpose-made captures. Other academic work (Maynooth/DCU, traffic lights) reports lower geolocation accuracy on crowdsourced Mapillary imagery because of camera-position noise. Failure modes specific to the street-light class (building-mounted lights, traffic signals, duplicates of the same lamp from different sequences) are NOT documented in any source I found; treat them as hypotheses to check on a sample, and consider de-duplicating points within a few metres.
answers.quote: To generate a map feature, an object must be detected in at least two (for traffic signs) or three (for all other point features) images.

answers.answer: Yes. In the web app (mapillary.com/app, login required): open the 'Map data' menu, pick the point class (Street Light) in the points drop-down, zoom to roughly city scale until the data renders and the 'Download' button is enabled, click 'Download'. Output: a GeoJSON feature collection of all visible features. Points and traffic signs must be downloaded separately; a date-range filter is available through 'Filters'. Limits: no numeric limit is documented; official guidance is that the web download suits a small area ('a town or a city neighborhood') and larger areas should use the API or Python SDK. The property names inside the downloaded GeoJSON are not documented. There is no equivalent documented no-code export for image coverage.
answers.quote: Click on the 'Download' button to get a feature collection of map data in GeoJSON format.

answers.answer: See the 'recipe' field. z14 tiles covering west=21.214, south=45.736, east=21.246, north=45.752: x = 9157..9158, y = 5845..5846 (4 tiles; row 5846 is needed only for the southernmost ~95 m, because the tile boundary lies at lat 45.73686). Route A (tiles) = 8 requests in total; route B (Graph bbox) = 8 cells of 0.008 x 0.008 deg per dataset.

result.recipe:
NOT RUN (no token). Placeholders: {TOKEN} = client token 'MLY|...|...' (URL-encode '|' as %7C if the client does not).
Model bbox: west=21.214 south=45.736 east=21.246 north=45.752.

ROUTE A - vector tiles (recommended; 8 requests; daily limit 50,000)
z14 tiles: x in {9157, 9158}, y in {5845, 5846}.
A1. Street lights, for each (x,y):
  GET https://tiles.mapillary.com/maps/vtp/mly_map_feature_point/2/14/{x}/{y}?access_token={TOKEN}
  Decode the MVT (pbf), layer 'point'; keep features where value == 'object--street-light'; convert tile coords to lon/lat; clip to the bbox.
  Properties kept: id, value, first_seen_at, last_seen_at (ms since epoch -> ISO date).
A2. Image coverage, for each (x,y):
  GET https://tiles.mapillary.com/maps/vtp/mly1_public/2/14/{x}/{y}?access_token={TOKEN}
  Layer 'image' (points): id, captured_at (ms), compass_angle, is_pano, sequence_id, creator_id, quality_score. Layer 'sequence' (lines): id, captured_at, is_pano.
  Optional: same path with mly1_computed_public for map-matched positions (better for snapping to street segments).
A3. Optional enrichment per lamp (direction and the contributing images with their dates):
  GET https://graph.mapillary.com/{MAP_FEATURE_ID}?access_token={TOKEN}&fields=id,geometry,object_value,first_seen_at,last_seen_at,aligned_direction,images.captured_at,images.is_pano,images.compass_angle
  or batched: GET https://graph.mapillary.com?ids={ID1},{ID2},...&fields=...&access_token={TOKEN}
Decoders: Python mapbox_vector_tile + mercantile, or mapillary-python-sdk: mly.interface.set_access_token(TOKEN); map_feature_points_in_bbox(bbox, filter_values=['object--street-light']); images_in_bbox(bbox).

ROUTE B - Graph API bbox search (no MVT decoder needed)
Split into 8 cells of 0.008 x 0.008 deg (safe under either reading of the 0.01-degree rule):
  lon edges: 21.214, 21.222, 21.230, 21.238, 21.246; lat edges: 45.736, 45.744, 45.752.
B1. Street lights, for each cell {w},{s},{e},{n}:
  GET https://graph.mapillary.com/map_features?access_token={TOKEN}&fields=id,geometry,object_value,object_type,first_seen_at,last_seen_at,aligned_direction&object_values=object--street-light&bbox={w},{s},{e},{n}&limit=2000
  Response: {"data":[...]}. If exactly 2000 rows come back, split that cell in four and repeat (no pagination for bbox search). De-duplicate by id across cells.
B2. Image coverage, for each cell:
  GET https://graph.mapillary.com/images?access_token={TOKEN}&fields=id,geometry,computed_geometry,captured_at,compass_angle,is_pano,sequence&bbox={w},{s},{e},{n}&limit=2000
  If 2000 rows: subdivide (the official FAQ uses z18 tile bounds) or slice with &start_captured_at=2019-01-01T00:00:00Z&end_captured_at=2020-01-01T00:00:00Z per year.
Header alternative for Graph calls: 'Authorization: OAuth {TOKEN}'.
On error code 4 'Application request limit reached' or HTTP 500: wait, then retry with a smaller cell.

USING THE RESULT HONESTLY
- Segment with no image within ~15-20 m: 'never captured' = no information.
- Segment with images but no street-light feature: weak negative only (a feature needs detections in >= 3 images); weaken further when image count is low or captured_at is old.
- Date every piece of evidence: lamp = last_seen_at; coverage = newest captured_at on the segment.
- Display the Mapillary logo with a link to mapillary.com wherever the derived data is shown; do not commit the raw export to the MIT repo - commit the fetch script.

NO-CODE FALLBACK: mapillary.com/app (logged in) -> 'Map data' -> points: Street Light -> zoom until rendered -> 'Download' -> GeoJSON (street lights only; no coverage export).

CITY-WIDE: enumerate z14 tiles for the city bbox (about 11 x 11 = 121 tiles per tileset for a rough Timisoara bbox 21.11-21.32 E, 45.69-45.84 N) and run A1 + A2 unchanged.
unconfirmed: That the client token is free of charge and issued instantly: the docs and blog describe a self-service 'Register Application' step with no approval and mention no price, but no official sentence says 'free' or states a waiting time. A 2020 blog line 'Mapillary's map data is now available for free, globally, to everyone' was seen only as a quotation in a forum post.
That client tokens never expire: only user (OAuth) tokens have a documented expiry; nothing is stated for client tokens.

That map features (derived points) are licensed CC BY-SA 4.0: the Terms apply CC BY-SA (no version number) to User Content, i.e. images; derived data is covered by the Terms with a logo-and-link attribution rule. The '4.0' version is not in the Terms or the help article.

That Mapillary-derived data can be mixed with ODbL data and redistributed outside OpenStreetMap: official text only covers contributing to OSM/Overture (Terms section 13, mapillary.com/osm). No official statement on ODbL compatibility or on redistribution in a third-party repository.
Any rule on caching or storing API results: none found in the Terms or API docs (neither a permission nor a prohibition).
The exact meaning of 'smaller than 0.01 degrees square' (0.01 sq deg of area versus 0.01 deg per side). The docs' own sample bbox (0.041 x 0.010 deg) implies area, but this was not tested.
Whether /map_features bbox search accepts aligned_direction and nested images.* fields in the search call (documented for the entity; the search sample shows only id, object_value).
Whether a dense z14 map-feature or image tile can silently drop features (no cap documented either way).

False positives of the street-light class (building or facade lights, traffic signals, illuminated signs) and duplicate points for one lamp: commonly reported informally, not documented officially or in the studies found.
The property names in the GeoJSON produced by the web app 'Download' button, and any feature-count limit of that download.
That most imagery in the Timisoara model area is older than 4 years: not checked (requires a token); verify from captured_at in the coverage tiles.
Affiliation of the SotM 2022 speaker (Said Turksever) with Mapillary/Meta: not stated on the talk page.
caveats: No authenticated call was made (no token), so every endpoint, parameter and limit is taken from documentation as fetched on 2026-11-14, not from a live test. The tile x/y range was computed locally with the standard Web Mercator formula.

Verbatim quotes come from the raw HTML of mapillary.com/developer/api-documentation (+ /points, /detections, /faq), mapillary.com/terms and help.mapillary.com articles fetched directly. The blog post, mapillary.com/osm and the State of the Map abstract were read through a summarising fetch tool, so their quotes are second-hand and should be re-checked before being cited publicly.

One help-centre lookup (object detections / computer vision articles) was stopped at the user's request to avoid spending more time; the help article 'Accessing imagery and data through the Mapillary API' turned out to contain no token instructions beyond a link to the API docs.
The API docs changed recently (bbox rule formalised 16 Jan 2026; quality_score added May 2026; on_foot added June 2026), so older tutorials and gists may contradict them; prefer the docs page.

M6 is a reading of the published terms, not legal advice. The safest setup is: fetch script in the repo, raw Mapillary export kept out of git, Mapillary logo + link and OSM attribution shown in the app.
The docs contain a small inconsistency: tile metadata lists ids as String while the prose lists them as int; treat ids as strings.

result.list_item_shape:
Top level: JSON array (22274 items for the 12-month window), NOT sorted by createdAt (neither ascending nor descending). Every item has exactly the same 9 keys:
- id: string (UUID), unique
- webconInstanceNr: string, pattern SZN9999-999999 (e.g. SZN2026-019882), unique
- createdAt: string, ISO 8601 with explicit offset +00:00 (UTC) on all 22274 items; fractional seconds have VARIABLE length, 1 to 6 digits (18671 with 6 digits, 1901 with 5, 1356 with 3, 175 with 4, 155 with 2, 14 with 1) - the parser must accept that. Min 2025-11-14T00:04:21.001+00:00, max 2026-11-13T23:41:18.972973+00:00 (consistent with the date window being applied in UTC; hour histogram peaks 06-17 UTC, i.e. daytime in Romanian local time UTC+2/+3).
- descriere: string (resident free text - do not republish)
- status: string (7 distinct values, no surrounding whitespace)
- categorii: object { nume: string } (single object, not an array)
- subcategorii: object { nume: string } (single object, not an array)
- locatie: null (1071 items) OR object { type: "Point", crs: { type: "name", properties: { name: "urn:ogc:def:crs:EPSG::4326" } }, coordinates: [lng: float, lat: float] } (21203 items). Missing location is null, not an empty object/string.
- files: array of { path: string } (0 items: 10379; 1: 6254; 2: 2588; 3+: 2817) OR null (236 items)
No updatedAt / closing date / street fields in the list.
GOTCHA: categorii.nume for lighting is "Iluminat public " WITH A TRAILING SPACE - an exact match on "Iluminat public" returns 0 rows; strip before comparing. Other names with stray whitespace: category "Probleme de integritate ", sub-categories " Registru spații verzi", "Deșeuri vegetale ", "Nereguli privind transportul public urban ".
There are 25 categories in total. Coordinates outliers: 12 reports (1 of them lighting) lie outside a rough Timisoara box (lat 45.68-45.83, lon 21.10-21.33); overall range lon 5.80..27.57, lat 44.45..49.57 - clip to the city.

4 cards fetched (lighting, inside the model bbox, 4 different statuses): SZN2026-019882 (Inregistrata), SZN2026-019089 (In lucru), SZN2026-018296 (Finalizata), SZN2026-001191 (Declinata competenta). All HTTP 200.
Card = one JSON object with 13 keys: id, descriere, locatie, strada, nrStrada, webconId, webconInstanceNr, createdAt, status, files, categorii, subcategorii, history.

Date format is the same as the list: ISO 8601 UTC with +00:00 and microseconds. Order is chronological ascending. The initial "Inregistrata" state is NOT logged: the Inregistrata card has history = [] (the registration time is the top-level createdAt).

GET https://servicii.primariatm.ro/api/nomenclator/strazi -> HTTP 200, application/json, 712,235 bytes (Cloudflare + Vercel, x-vercel-cache HIT, Cache-Control public, max-age=0). Top level is an OBJECT, not an array: { strazi: [1370 rows], activeCount: 1365 }.
Row fields (20, same in every row): id (int), codWebcon (str), codGis (str; empty in 20 rows, unique in the other 1350), numarInstanta (str, e.g. NSTR2022-000002), stare (str: Existenta 1365, Dezafectata 5), denumireCompleta, denumireCompletaFaraDiacritice, numeActual, numeActualFaraDiacritice, numeAnterior, numeAnteriorFaraDiacritice, tipArtera, cartier, careuGhid, actAn, dataHcl, nrImparMin, nrImparMax, nrParMin, nrParMax (all str). No geometry / coordinates.
Name formats:
- denumireCompleta = full name WITH type prefix and WITH diacritics, title case: "Strada Cluj", "Bulevardul Vasile Pârvan", "Piața Victoriei". Romanian letters use the correct comma-below code points (ș U+0219, ț U+021B; no cedilla variants), plus ă â î and a few foreign letters (ć ö é ő ó ü á ä š ô ž).
- tipArtera values: Strada 1131, Intrarea 96, Aleea 45, Piața 44, Bulevardul 28, Calea 15, Splaiul 9, Scuarul 1, empty 1 (row "Rozelor").
- numeActual = bare name WITHOUT prefix and often without honorific: denumireCompleta equals tipArtera + " " + numeActual in only 1226 of 1370 rows; the rest insert a title that numeActual drops ("Bulevardul Regele Ferdinand I" vs numeActual "Ferdinand I"; "Bulevardul General Ion Dragalina" vs "Ion Dragalina"; "Aleea Martir ..." vs the person name). So match on denumireCompleta, not on tipArtera + numeActual.
- *FaraDiacritice fields are a mostly-ASCII copy but NOT reliable: 5 rows still contain non-ASCII ("Piața Petofi Sandor", "Strada Dositej Obradović", "Strada János Bolyai", "Strada Niccoló Paganini", "Strada Vuk St. Karadžić") and 26 rows differ from a plain accent-fold of denumireCompleta (21 because denumireCompleta carries the suffix " - denumire provizorie" that the diacritic-free field omits). Do your own Unicode folding.
- Quirks: particles are title-cased ("De" 13, "La" 6, "Cel" 4, "Din" 3, "Și" 1: "Bulevardul Eroilor De La Tisa", "Strada Mircea Cel Bătrân", "Bulevardul Revoluției Din 1989"); 54 names contain dotted abbreviations with a space after each dot ("Aleea F. C. Ripensia", "Strada Dr. ...", "Strada Acad. ...", "Strada Arh. ...", "Strada J. H. Pestalozzi"); titles appear both abbreviated and spelled out (Martir 60, Dr. 21, General 11, Acad. 7, Arh. 5, Prof. 5, Profesor 3, Mitropolit 5, Sfântul 3, Sf. 1, Lt. 1); 4 names carry a year in parentheses ("Strada Martir Conciatu (1918)"); 35 hyphenated; one duplicated active full name ("Calea Moșniței" twice).
- numeAnterior (former name) differs from numeActual in 874 rows, sometimes just the reversed order ("Pârvan Vasile"), sometimes a real old name ("Sportivilor" for Aleea F. C. Ripensia) or free text.
District / zone field: YES but dirty - cartier is free text with 361 distinct values and inconsistent spellings (e.g. "Campus Universitar" 22 rows, "Campus Univ." 10, "Campus Univ.-Piața Crucii" 3, "Campus Univ. Stadion" 1, "Campus, P-Ța Crucii, Stad." 1; 21 rows empty); 40 rows mention Campus. careuGhid is a printed-map grid reference ("E5, E6"). Usable as a hint only, not as a filter key.

result.name_matching_verdict:
Basis: 4 card strada strings (S3) plus the full street register (S5). OSM names were NOT fetched in this run; the OSM side below rests on the convention stated in the task ("Strada Cluj", "Bulevardul Vasile Pârvan").
Findings: card strada = register denumireCompleta, exact string match in 4 of 4, so the practical chain is strada -> register row (gives codGis, stare, former name) -> OSM name. The register's full name already has the same structure as OSM (type prefix + name), so no prefix has to be added or removed; the hard part is small spelling differences.
Normalisation needed on both sides before comparing:
1. Unicode NFKC, then fold diacritics yourself (NFD, drop combining marks; also map cedilla ş/ţ to s/t in case OSM has legacy forms). Do not rely on the register's *FaraDiacritice fields (5 rows still non-ASCII) and do not assume strada has diacritics (unverified).
2. Case-fold. This is mandatory: the register title-cases particles ("Eroilor De La Tisa", "Mircea Cel Bătrân", "Revoluției Din 1989", 27 particle occurrences) where normal Romanian orthography uses lower case.
3. Collapse whitespace and normalise dotted abbreviations: remove the space after single-letter initials and compare with dots stripped ("F. C. Ripensia" vs "F.C. Ripensia" vs "FC Ripensia"; "J. H. Pestalozzi"; "I. C. Brătianu"). 54 register names are affected.
4. Keep the type prefix as a separate token and canonicalise it (Strada/Str., Bulevardul/Bd./B-dul/Bv., Piața/P-ța, Calea, Aleea, Intrarea, Splaiul, Scuarul). Do not drop it blindly: the bare name is ambiguous in a few cases ("Bulevardul Iuliu Maniu" and "Piața Iuliu Maniu" both exist), but allow a prefix-agnostic fallback because type can differ between sources.
5. Titles: expand or strip a small list on both sides before comparing (Dr./Doctor, Acad./Academician, Arh./Arhitect, Prof./Profesor, Gen./General, Lt., Sf./Sfântul/Sfânta, Martir, Regele, Mitropolit, Episcop). The register itself is inconsistent (Prof. 5 vs Profesor 3; Sf. 1 vs Sfântul 3) and its numeActual drops the title entirely in 144 rows.
6. Strip register-only decorations: " - denumire provizorie" (21 rows) and year suffixes in parentheses ("(1918)", 4 rows).
7. Fallbacks for leftovers: compare against numeAnterior (former names, 874 rows differ) and against OSM old_name/alt_name; then a token-set / edit-distance match restricted to candidates near the report point.
Reliability: for ordinary names (the large majority: "Strada Cluj", "Strada Daliei", "Bulevardul Vasile Pârvan", "Bulevardul Liviu Rebreanu", "Splaiul Tudor Vladimirescu") steps 1-2 alone should give exact equality; names with particles, initials or titles need steps 3-5; expect a small manual alias table for the model area (40 register rows mention Campus, so this is checkable by hand in minutes). Not measured: the actual match rate against OSM. More important for the design: every lighting report used for scoring already has coordinates (1550 of 1607), so the primary join to street segments should be spatial (nearest segment within a tolerance), with strada used as a cross-check / tie-breaker at junctions and for the 57 reports without coordinates - and strada costs one card request per report.

result.gis_lighting_layers:
Unknown from public static files - no lighting layer name was found, and the layer catalogue could not be read without calling the GIS API (not done). 4 requests used:
1. https://harta.primariatm.ro/ -> HTTP 200, Server: Vercel, a Next.js page (title "Municipiul Timișoara - Acasă") that only wraps an iframe: https://app.urbis.primariatm.ro/embed/137547f2-ed11-4fb2-8238-6bcc83de9cf4
2. that embed page -> HTTP 200, 4 KB shell of a single-page app ("Initializing application..."), scripts /set-config.js and /assets/index-6a6d135c.js.
3. /set-config.js -> 42 bytes: window.env = {} (no configuration, no layer list).
4. /assets/index-6a6d135c.js -> 6.45 MB application bundle.
Technology (from the bundle): a proprietary platform named "Urbis Web Portal" v2.0 (APP_ENV "live-k8s-tm"), built as a Vue + Vite single-page app on Mapbox GL JS (with mapbox-gl-draw and deck.gl layer types). Backend hosts referenced: https://api.urbis.primariatm.ro/api/v1/ and /api/v2/, https://sync-api.urbis.primariatm.ro, https://tile-server.urbis.primariatm.ro (vector/raster tiles), glyphs at /api/v1/utils/fonts/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf; the vendor domains listed alongside are gis-solution.ro and sync-map.com ("SyncMap"). It is NOT ArcGIS, GeoServer or QGIS Server (no arcgis/geoserver/qgis strings; WMS/WMTS/WFS client settings exist but default to empty).
Lighting: the strings iluminat, stalp/stâlp and corpuri do not occur in the page, the config or the bundle. The layer catalogue for the embed is loaded at runtime from api.urbis.primariatm.ro and is not in any static file, so which layers the city publishes was not determined. One relevant hint: the platform's layer-type enumeration contains a dedicated type "StreetLight" (id 277, next to Traffic, Stations, Routes, PointOfInterest, Vehicles) - the software supports a street-light layer type, which says nothing about whether Timisoara has loaded one.
What to ask the city for: (a) whether the Urbis GIS holds a public-lighting layer (lamp posts / corpuri de iluminat / stâlpi, or the operator's inventory) and an export of it as GeoJSON or CSV with coordinates, lamp type and commissioning status, at least for the university district; (b) if not, the lighting operator's inventory or the list of streets with modernised lighting; (c) permission and an endpoint for read access to the relevant Urbis layer. To see the public layer list without touching the API programmatically, a team member can open harta.primariatm.ro in a browser and read the layer panel.
caveats: All counts are a live snapshot taken 2026-11-14 about 03:25 UTC; the team's figures (21527 total, 1479 lighting with coordinates) were not reproduced (22274 and 1550) and the difference is unexplained - a simple earlier-snapshot cut does not reproduce it (first 21527 reports by date contain 1455 lighting with coordinates).

The lighting category string has a trailing space ("Iluminat public "); an exact match on the documented name returns zero rows. A browser-console count that matched without trimming would have had to use includes()/startsWith - worth checking how the team filtered.

Card findings rest on 4 cards only (the allowed maximum): strada was non-empty in 4 of 4, none of the 4 street names contains diacritics, so 'strada can be empty' and 'strada carries diacritics' are both unverified. No Rezolvata, Declinat competenta or Asteapta clarificari card was fetched; the history of those statuses is unverified.

Closing dates exist only in cards (history), one request per report; the list has no closing or update date. Age statistics therefore use createdAt only, and 'In lucru' durations are ages of still-open reports, not time-to-fix.

The date window appears to be applied in UTC (min createdAt 2025-11-14T00:04Z, max 2026-11-13T23:41Z) but this is an inference from the data, not a documented fact; local time in Timisoara is UTC+2 or UTC+3, so day boundaries differ by 2-3 hours.

The clustering figure is a proxy: 30 m / 14 days single-linkage on report pins; pins are placed by residents on a map and their positional accuracy was not assessed. 59 lighting reports share identical coordinates with another one.

iluminat_min.geojson contains all 1550 lighting reports with coordinates, including 1 point outside a rough Timisoara box; clip before use. It carries webconInstanceNr, which lets anyone look up the public card (with resident text) - do not publish the file as-is if that matters; drop the number or keep it server-side.

OSM and Mapillary were not queried in this run (out of scope for this step); the name-matching verdict's OSM side relies on the convention stated in the task, and no match rate against OSM was measured.
The city guide page (ghid-pmt.vercel.app/unihack) was not fetched in this run; statements about what is documented come from the task text. No undocumented query parameters were probed.

City GIS: the public layer catalogue was not read - it is served at runtime by api.urbis.primariatm.ro, which was deliberately not called (request budget of 4 used on page, embed, config and bundle; the guide says the GIS has no public API). 'No lighting layer' is therefore NOT established, only 'not visible in static files'. The bundle contains public client-side keys (map token, captcha site key); they were not reproduced and should not be reused.
CKAN: dataset contents (CSV files) were not downloaded; the 'none found' verdict is based on the complete catalogue metadata (36 datasets).

Privacy: raw responses with resident text and photo paths are stored only under the data folder listed in files. While checking the S1 response, the first ~120 bytes of one raw item (start of one report's text) were echoed to this agent's own tool log; nothing of it is included in this answer or written elsewhere.

Nothing was created or modified under c:/Users/Timur/F1/Unihack. No Python packages were installed (standard library only). Requests to sesizari.primariatm.ro: 7 of the allowed 12, sequential, at least 2 s apart.
